attractionDescriptions.Manuel Antonio National Park: On the central Pacific coast, this protected area brings tropical forest close to sandy beaches. Forest trails and coastal viewpoints offer opportunities to observe wildlife without leaving marked routes.
attractionDescriptions.Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve: Moisture-laden cloud forest supports orchids, epiphytes and a rich variety of birds in this mountain reserve. Walking paths introduce the layered vegetation of Costa Rica's highland forests.
attractionDescriptions.Tortuguero National Park: Caribbean lowland forests, canals and wetlands form the heart of this protected area. Its coast is an important nesting habitat for green turtles, with visits governed by conservation rules.
attractionDescriptions.La Fortuna Waterfall: Near La Fortuna, this tall waterfall drops into a forested gorge. A substantial stairway leads toward the lower viewing area, while the surrounding reserve protects the river landscape.
attractionDescriptions.Poás Volcano National Park: This highland national park protects an active volcanic crater and surrounding cloud forest. Views and visitor access depend on weather, volcanic conditions and the park authority's current rules.

costa-rica.cultureIntro: San José's National Theatre reflects the capital's nineteenth-century cultural ambitions, while the National Museum explores Costa Rican history. The Central Market offers a closer look at everyday food and commerce.
costa-rica.foodIntro: Rice, beans, root vegetables and fresh produce underpin home-style dishes commonly served in Costa Rica's small local restaurants, known as sodas.
costa-rica.activitiesIntro: Explore waterfall paths, forest suspension bridges and the distinctive turquoise river landscape of Tenorio's Río Celeste.
costa-rica.nightlifeIntro: San José's performance venues include the Teatro Popular Melico Salazar, while Jacó's Pacific waterfront draws visitors for sunset and evening dining.

activityDescriptions.La Paz Waterfall Gardens: Follow the managed forest paths to viewpoints of several waterfalls, including La Paz and Magia Blanca, within this privately operated nature attraction.
activityDescriptions.Arenal hanging bridges: Walk forest trails and suspension bridges around Arenal to observe different levels of the rainforest, looking for birds and plants along the way.
activityDescriptions.Río Celeste hiking: Follow designated trails in Tenorio Volcano National Park to the waterfall and blue river viewpoints, respecting the protected area's access and conservation rules.

foodDescriptions.Gallo pinto: Rice and beans are cooked together with ingredients such as onion, sweet pepper and coriander, often for breakfast.
foodDescriptions.Casado: This typical lunch plate brings together rice, beans, salad or vegetables and a chosen protein, with accompaniments varying by kitchen.
foodDescriptions.Chifrijo: This layered bowl combines rice, beans and pieces of pork with pico de gallo, usually accompanied by tortilla chips.
foodDescriptions.Olla de carne: This home-style beef stew includes substantial vegetables and roots such as cassava, potatoes, taro and plantain.

jamaica.intro: Jamaica combines Caribbean beaches and terraced waterfalls with a powerful musical heritage. Kingston's museums and historic homes reveal the people and creative traditions behind the island's global influence.
jamaica.tagline: Reggae roots, waterfall country and Caribbean flavor

sources.title: Jamaica Information Service: country and parish facts
Visit Jamaica: language and visitor information
Visit Jamaica: museums and Port Royal
Visit Jamaica: Devon House and Bob Marley Museum
Visit Jamaica: Kingston and musical heritage

attractionDescriptions.Dunn's River Falls: Near Ocho Rios, water cascades down a series of natural limestone terraces toward the Caribbean Sea. The forested setting and beach below make this a distinctive coastal waterfall landscape.
attractionDescriptions.Hope Botanical Gardens: Also known as the Royal Botanical Gardens, this large green space lies in urban St. Andrew. Specialized gardens, mature trees and ornamental plantings provide a quieter side of Kingston.
attractionDescriptions.Bob Marley Museum: Marley's former home at 56 Hope Road in Kingston preserves the setting where he lived and worked. Exhibits introduce the musician's life, recordings and enduring cultural influence.
attractionDescriptions.Devon House: Built in 1881 for George Stiebel, Jamaica's first Black millionaire, this Kingston mansion reflects nineteenth-century domestic life. The landscaped grounds also include shops and a well-known ice-cream stop.
attractionDescriptions.Port Royal: At the entrance to Kingston Harbour, Port Royal recalls the island's maritime and colonial history. Fort Charles and surviving historic structures help explain the town's strategic importance.

jamaica.cultureIntro: Reggae and dancehall are central to Jamaica's creative identity, with Kingston recognized as a UNESCO Creative City of Music. The National Gallery and Institute of Jamaica broaden the story through art and heritage collections.
jamaica.foodIntro: Jamaican cooking layers African, European and Asian influences through dishes such as jerk chicken, ackee and saltfish, patties and rice and peas.
jamaica.activitiesIntro: Balance Montego Bay's beach time with Kingston's urban green spaces and the garden setting around YS Falls.
jamaica.nightlifeIntro: Kingston's reggae and dancehall scene brings music into the evening, while Negril's west-facing coast provides a setting for sunset views.

activityDescriptions.Doctor's Cave Beach Club: Spend time on the sand and swim in designated areas at this established Montego Bay beach club, following current beach conditions and staff guidance.
activityDescriptions.Emancipation Park, Kingston: Walk the landscaped paths, see the Redemption Song sculpture and spend time in a public park commemorating emancipation from slavery.
activityDescriptions.YS Falls: Explore garden paths and waterfall viewpoints on Jamaica's South Coast, with seven cascades set within a working estate landscape.

foodDescriptions.Ackee and saltfish: Jamaica's national dish combines cooked ackee with salted cod, onion, tomato and seasoning.
foodDescriptions.Jamaican jerk chicken: Chicken is seasoned with a spicy aromatic mixture commonly including allspice and Scotch bonnet pepper, then cooked for a smoky flavor.
foodDescriptions.Jamaican patty: A flaky golden pastry encloses a savory filling, often seasoned beef, with chicken and vegetable versions also common.
foodDescriptions.Jamaican rice and peas: Rice cooks with beans or pigeon peas, coconut milk and seasonings to make a staple accompaniment.

brazil.intro: Atlantic beaches, Amazon forest and powerful waterfalls give Brazil an extraordinary range of landscapes. In Rio and Salvador, samba, capoeira and distinctive regional cooking bring the country's cultural history into everyday life.
brazil.tagline: Coastal cities, forest landscapes and the rhythms of samba

sources.title: Bahia heritage institute: Baianas do Acarajé
Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden: Visiting the arboretum
Bahia rural development department: Pão de queijo

attractionDescriptions.Christ the Redeemer (statue): The Art Deco figure stands on Corcovado above Rio de Janeiro, with its outstretched arms facing the city. Its mountain setting brings together views of Guanabara Bay, beaches and forest.
attractionDescriptions.Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro: Copacabana's broad beach curves along one of Rio's best-known neighbourhoods. The patterned promenade, waterfront buildings and beach sports make this a distinctive meeting point between city life and the Atlantic.
attractionDescriptions.Iguazu Falls: The Iguaçu River drops over a vast series of falls on the border with Argentina. Brazil's national park provides sweeping views of the cascades within an important Atlantic Forest landscape.
attractionDescriptions.Brasília Cathedral: Oscar Niemeyer's cathedral is one of Brasília's signature modernist buildings. Curving concrete supports form a crown around a light-filled interior, expressing the experimental architecture of Brazil's planned capital.
attractionDescriptions.Escadaria Selarón: Artist Jorge Selarón transformed these steps between Lapa and Santa Teresa into a colourful mosaic. Tiles from many countries cover the staircase, making it a public artwork woven into Rio's streets.

brazil.cultureIntro: Rio's samba schools and Bahia's capoeira traditions express distinct strands of Afro-Brazilian culture. Salvador's Pelourinho also connects architecture, music and the heritage of its Black communities.
brazil.foodIntro: Cassava, beans, seafood and regional ingredients such as dendê palm oil connect Brazil's Indigenous, African and European culinary influences.
brazil.activitiesIntro: Rio's mountain transport and botanical garden offer several ways to see how the city meets its forested hills.
brazil.nightlifeIntro: Rio's evenings include Lapa's samba venues, while the Sambadrome becomes a major stage for samba-school parades during Carnival.

activityDescriptions.Sugarloaf Cable Car: Ride the cable car via Morro da Urca to Sugarloaf for views across Guanabara Bay, Rio's beaches and the surrounding mountains.
activityDescriptions.Corcovado Rack Railway: Travel up Corcovado through Tijuca's forest on the rack railway, then continue to the Christ the Redeemer viewing area.
activityDescriptions.Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro: Explore the arboretum's paths and plant collections to discover a quieter, leafy side of Rio beneath the Corcovado hills.

foodDescriptions.Feijoada brasileira: Feijoada is a slow-cooked stew of beans and meats, commonly made with black beans and pork and served with rice and accompaniments.
foodDescriptions.Pão de queijo: These small cheese breads use cassava starch, giving the baked crust and soft centre their characteristic texture.
foodDescriptions.Moqueca baiana: Bahia's moqueca is a fish or seafood stew flavoured with coconut milk and dendê palm oil.
foodDescriptions.Acarajé: Acarajé is a fritter of black-eyed peas and onion fried in dendê oil, often split and filled with shrimp, vatapá and other accompaniments.

peru.intro: Peru links Pacific coast, Andean mountains and Amazon rainforest with the remains of many ancient societies. Lima's food traditions and the Inca landscapes around Cusco make contrasting starting points for exploring the country.
peru.tagline: Andean stonework, coastal flavours and living traditions
peru.languages: Spanish; Quechua, Aymara and other Indigenous languages

sources.title: Peru Travel: Lima's museums and culture

attractionDescriptions.Plaza Mayor, Lima: Lima's historic main square is framed by the cathedral, Government Palace and arcaded civic buildings. It anchors a World Heritage city centre shaped by the Spanish colonial period.
attractionDescriptions.Larco Museum: Set in Lima's Pueblo Libre district, the Larco Museum presents pre-Columbian art and archaeology. Its ceramic collections introduce the societies that flourished in Peru long before the Inca Empire.
attractionDescriptions.Machu Picchu: Inca terraces and carefully fitted stone buildings occupy a mountain ridge above the Urubamba valley. The site combines agricultural and urban sectors within a protected Andean landscape recognised by UNESCO.
attractionDescriptions.Sacsayhuamán: Above Cusco, Sacsayhuamán is known for monumental stone walls assembled from immense, closely fitted blocks. Its archaeological remains form part of the wider landscape of the former Inca capital.
attractionDescriptions.Nazca Lines: Animals, geometric shapes and long lines were traced into southern Peru's desert surface by pre-Hispanic communities. These enormous geoglyphs form a World Heritage landscape whose full purposes remain debated.

peru.cultureIntro: Cusco's Inti Raymi celebrates the Inca sun tradition, while Puno's Virgen de la Candelaria festival brings together music, dance and religious devotion. Quechua and Aymara communities sustain important strands of living Andean culture.
peru.foodIntro: Peruvian cooking draws on coastal seafood, Andean crops and Indigenous, African, European and Asian culinary traditions.
peru.activitiesIntro: Explore Lima's Pacific-facing neighbourhoods or follow the Inca routes that connect archaeological sites in the Andes.
peru.nightlifeIntro: Barranco's streets and arts venues offer an evening atmosphere distinct from Lima's illuminated fountain displays at the Circuito Mágico del Agua.

activityDescriptions.Larcomar: Browse the shops and restaurants of this open-air complex built into Miraflores' cliffs, with viewpoints over Lima's Pacific coastline.
activityDescriptions.Inca Trail to Machu Picchu: Follow a permitted guided route through Andean scenery and Inca archaeological sites toward Machu Picchu, with advance planning for access and altitude.
activityDescriptions.Paragliding in Miraflores: Watch paragliders above Miraflores' coastal cliffs, or arrange a tandem flight with a qualified operator when local flying conditions permit.

foodDescriptions.Peruvian ceviche: Peruvian ceviche combines raw fish marinated in citrus juice with chilli and onion, often accompanied by sweet potato and corn.
foodDescriptions.Lomo saltado: This Chinese-influenced stir-fry combines beef, onion, tomato and soy sauce, usually served with both rice and fried potatoes.
foodDescriptions.Ají de gallina: Shredded chicken is coated in a creamy ají pepper sauce thickened with bread and milk, commonly served with rice and potatoes.
foodDescriptions.Causa limeña: Causa layers seasoned mashed potato around fillings such as chicken, seafood or avocado and is served cold.

argentina.intro: Argentina stretches from subtropical forest at Iguazú to glaciers and windswept landscapes in Patagonia. Buenos Aires adds grand theatres, neighbourhood football and tango to a country with strong regional food and wine traditions.
argentina.tagline: Tango streets, Andean vineyards and Patagonia's vast landscapes
argentina.languages: Spanish; Indigenous languages are also spoken

sources.title: Buenos Aires tourism: Plaza de Mayo and Caminito
Visit Argentina: Los Glaciares National Park
Buenos Aires tourism: Boca Juniors museum

attractionDescriptions.Plaza de Mayo: Buenos Aires' oldest square has been a setting for major political events and public demonstrations. The Casa Rosada, Metropolitan Cathedral and historic Cabildo stand around its edges.
attractionDescriptions.Caminito: Caminito is a short street museum in La Boca, known for colourful corrugated-metal houses and its connection with artist Benito Quinquela Martín. Its streetscape recalls the neighbourhood's working-class port history.
attractionDescriptions.Perito Moreno Glacier: A great ice front reaches Lago Argentino within Los Glaciares National Park. Viewing walkways reveal the glacier's crevassed surface and the meeting point between ice, lake and Patagonian forest.
attractionDescriptions.Recoleta Cemetery: Ornate mausoleums and sculpted memorials form a compact city of tombs in Buenos Aires. Eva Perón's resting place is among the cemetery's best-known sites, alongside many other prominent Argentines.
attractionDescriptions.Iguazu National Park: Subtropical forest surrounds the Argentine side of the Iguazú waterfalls. The park protects a rich natural landscape, with visitor walkways offering different perspectives on the river and its cascades.

argentina.cultureIntro: Tango grew from the urban cultures of the Río de la Plata and remains closely associated with Buenos Aires. Theatre, visual art and football also shape the capital's neighbourhood identities.
argentina.foodIntro: Argentine food ranges from shared asado grills and regional empanadas to dulce de leche sweets, with Mendoza central to its wine culture.
argentina.activitiesIntro: Football heritage, river islands and Andean vineyards offer three different ways into Argentina's landscapes and local life.
argentina.nightlifeIntro: Buenos Aires offers tango performances and late dining, while Puerto Madero's converted docks provide a waterfront setting for an evening stroll.

activityDescriptions.La Bombonera: Discover Boca Juniors' football history through the stadium museum and available visitor experiences in the club's La Boca neighbourhood.
activityDescriptions.Tigre Delta: Take an organised boat excursion from Tigre through the Paraná Delta's channels to see riverside homes, islands and wetland vegetation.
activityDescriptions.Mendoza vineyards: Visit a Mendoza winery to learn about grape growing and winemaking in the dry Andean foothills, where irrigation sustains the vineyards.

foodDescriptions.Asado argentino: Asado is both a meal of meats cooked over a grill or embers and a social gathering centred on sharing the food.
foodDescriptions.Empanadas argentinas: These filled pastry turnovers vary by province, with seasoned meat among the most familiar fillings and baking or frying used in different traditions.
foodDescriptions.Choripán: Choripán pairs grilled chorizo sausage with bread and is often dressed with chimichurri.
foodDescriptions.Alfajor argentino: An alfajor sandwiches a sweet filling, commonly dulce de leche, between biscuits, with chocolate or other coatings in many versions.

chile.intro: Chile runs between the Andes and the Pacific, taking in Atacama desert landscapes and the lakes and glaciers of Patagonia. Santiago's historic centre and Rapa Nui's monumental heritage reveal very different chapters of the country's story.
chile.tagline: Desert skies, Pacific culture and Patagonia's granite peaks
chile.languages: Spanish; Indigenous languages include Mapudungun and Rapa Nui

sources.title: Chile Travel: Torres del Paine National Park

attractionDescriptions.Santa Lucía Hill: This landscaped rocky hill rises within central Santiago, offering paths, terraces and city views. It is closely associated with the Spanish foundation of Santiago in 1541.
attractionDescriptions.Plaza de Armas, Santiago: Santiago's main square forms the heart of its historic centre. The Metropolitan Cathedral and important civic buildings frame a public space that connects the city's colonial origins with contemporary street life.
attractionDescriptions.Torres del Paine National Park: Granite towers and the Cuernos del Paine rise above lakes, glaciers, forest and Patagonian steppe. The national park's contrasting habitats support wildlife including guanacos, condors and pumas.
attractionDescriptions.Rapa Nui National Park: The park preserves monumental moai statues, ceremonial platforms and other traces of Rapa Nui society. Its World Heritage landscape records the distinctive sculpture and architecture developed by the island's Polynesian people.
attractionDescriptions.Salar de Atacama: Chile's largest salt flat lies near San Pedro de Atacama. Salt crusts, lagoons and surrounding desert mountains create a stark landscape, with protected wetland areas providing habitat for flamingos.

chile.cultureIntro: Chile's cultural landscape includes Mapuche traditions, Rapa Nui's Polynesian heritage and northern festivals such as La Tirana. Santiago's museums and Pablo Neruda's La Chascona add art and literature to the picture.
chile.foodIntro: Corn, seafood, pastoral cooking and regional produce shape a cuisine that includes pino-filled empanadas and dishes from both coast and countryside.
chile.activitiesIntro: Santiago's hillside transport, Andean ski areas and Atacama's geothermal landscapes show the range of experiences across Chile.
chile.nightlifeIntro: Santiago's restaurants and performance venues bring life to the evening, with viewpoints such as Sky Costanera offering another perspective on the illuminated city.

activityDescriptions.Santiago Funicular: Ride the historic funicular up San Cristóbal Hill in Santiago's Metropolitan Park, then explore the viewpoints and surrounding park paths.
activityDescriptions.El Tatio: Visit the high-altitude geothermal field with an organised excursion to observe steam vents and geysers from designated areas.
activityDescriptions.Valle Nevado: Visit this Andean mountain resort above Santiago for alpine scenery and seasonal skiing or snowboarding when snow conditions and operations allow.

foodDescriptions.Pastel de choclo: A sweetcorn topping covers a savoury filling that commonly includes beef and onion, with chicken, egg, olives or raisins in different preparations.
foodDescriptions.Empanada de pino: This Chilean pastry encloses a pino filling of seasoned beef and onion, commonly joined by egg and an olive.
foodDescriptions.Chorrillana: Chorrillana piles fried potatoes with meat and other toppings, often including sausage, onion and egg.
foodDescriptions.Mote con huesillo: Cooked wheat grains and dried peaches are served cold in a sweet spiced syrup, making a drink substantial enough to eat with a spoon.

colombia.intro: Colombia's Caribbean shores, Andean cities and tropical forests create striking changes of landscape and climate. Cartagena's fortifications and Bogotá's museums introduce a country shaped by Indigenous, African and European histories.
colombia.tagline: Caribbean fortresses, mountain cities and many regional flavours
colombia.languages: Spanish; more than 60 Indigenous languages are also spoken

sources.title: Colombia Travel: Religious and spiritual tourism

attractionDescriptions.Castillo San Felipe de Barajas: Built on Cartagena's San Lázaro hill, this Spanish colonial fortress defended the city's landward approach. Its ramps, walls and underground passages reveal the scale of Cartagena's historic military defences.
attractionDescriptions.Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá: A sequence of chapels and sculpted religious spaces occupies tunnels in a working salt-mining landscape near Bogotá. The underground sanctuary connects modern devotional architecture with Zipaquirá's long history of salt extraction.
attractionDescriptions.Monserrate: This mountain sanctuary rises above Bogotá and is both a pilgrimage destination and a viewpoint. Its church, gardens and transport routes bring visitors above the dense city on the plateau.
attractionDescriptions.Ciudad Perdida: Stone terraces and stairways survive in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta's tropical forest. The archaeological site is associated with the Tairona and lies within a living Indigenous cultural landscape.
attractionDescriptions.Cartagena Cathedral: The Cathedral of Santa Catalina de Alejandría stands in Cartagena's historic centre near Parque Bolívar. Construction began in the sixteenth century, and its prominent tower helps define the old city's skyline.

colombia.cultureIntro: Cartagena's palenquera traditions connect the city with Afro-Colombian heritage, while Bogotá's Gold Museum presents the artistry of pre-Hispanic societies. Fernando Botero's work adds a distinct modern artistic voice.
colombia.foodIntro: Colombian food changes markedly by region, from Caribbean fried arepas to Bogotá's potato soups and the generous platters of the paisa region.
colombia.activitiesIntro: Follow Cartagena's walls, ride above Medellín's hills or climb Guatapé's rock for different views of Colombian settlement and landscape.
colombia.nightlifeIntro: Cartagena's historic squares provide settings for evening dining and music, while Caribbean rhythms are an important part of the city's cultural life.

activityDescriptions.Walls of Cartagena: Walk accessible sections of Cartagena's historic defensive walls to see the Caribbean, old-city rooftops and the scale of its colonial fortifications.
activityDescriptions.Medellín Metrocable: Use Medellín's aerial cable transport to see the city spread across its valley and gain a different perspective on hillside neighbourhoods.
activityDescriptions.El Peñón de Guatapé: Climb the constructed stairway on this immense rock for views over the islands and inlets of the surrounding reservoir.

foodDescriptions.Bandeja paisa: This substantial platter commonly combines beans, rice, meat, pork crackling, plantain, egg, avocado and an arepa.
foodDescriptions.Ajiaco santafereño: Bogotá's ajiaco is a chicken soup made with several kinds of potato and the herb guascas, often served with corn and accompaniments.
foodDescriptions.Arepa de huevo: A Caribbean coastal speciality, arepa de huevo is a fried corn cake with an egg enclosed inside.
foodDescriptions.Pandebono: Pandebono is a small cheese bread associated with Valle del Cauca, typically made using cheese and starch-based dough.

australia.intro: Australia brings together tropical reefs, vast inland landscapes and cities set around beaches and harbours. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures connect people with Country across a continent of remarkable regional variety.
australia.tagline: Harbour cities, coral reefs and ancient connections to Country
australia.languages: English is the main language; many Indigenous and community languages

sources.title: Tourism Australia: Currency and travel tips
Tourism Australia: Sydney and reef itinerary
Australian War Memorial: Anzac biscuit recipes

attractionDescriptions.Sydney Opera House: Jørn Utzon's sculptural performing-arts complex occupies Bennelong Point on Sydney Harbour. Its shell-like roof forms are internationally recognised, while the building's theatres host a wide range of performances.
attractionDescriptions.Bondi Beach: This sandy ocean beach sits among Sydney's eastern suburbs and has a strong surfing and lifesaving identity. The promenade and coastal walking route connect its seafront with neighbouring bays.
attractionDescriptions.Great Barrier Reef: Off Queensland, this immense reef system contains coral reefs, islands and diverse marine habitats. Boat-based experiences introduce its underwater landscapes, with conservation central to visiting this World Heritage ecosystem.
attractionDescriptions.Sydney Harbour Bridge: The steel arch bridge links central Sydney with the North Shore across the harbour. Its pedestrian route offers a close view of the structure and perspectives toward the Opera House.
attractionDescriptions.Kakadu National Park: Wetlands, sandstone escarpments and Aboriginal rock-art sites form part of Kakadu's World Heritage landscape. Bininj and Mungguy Traditional Owners maintain deep cultural connections with this seasonally changing country.

australia.cultureIntro: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples hold diverse cultural traditions and connections to Country. Major museums and galleries also present the art, natural history and many communities of contemporary Australia.
australia.foodIntro: Australian food includes bakery classics and everyday favourites alongside regional produce, Indigenous ingredients and the cooking traditions of many migrant communities.
australia.activitiesIntro: Harbour ferries, coastal road journeys and rainforest railways make the journey itself part of exploring Australia.
australia.nightlifeIntro: Sydney's Circular Quay and Darling Harbour combine waterfront dining, cultural venues and evening views of the city.

activityDescriptions.Manly ferry: Cross Sydney Harbour by ferry to Manly, watching the Opera House, Harbour Bridge and bays before exploring the beachside suburb.
activityDescriptions.Great Ocean Road: Travel Victoria's coastal route between seaside towns, beaches and forest, stopping at designated viewpoints to see the limestone coast.
activityDescriptions.Kuranda Scenic Railway: Ride the heritage railway between Cairns and Kuranda through tropical rainforest, with views of mountain scenery and Barron Gorge.

foodDescriptions.Lamington: A lamington is a square of sponge cake coated with chocolate icing and desiccated coconut, sometimes filled with jam or cream.
foodDescriptions.ANZAC biscuit: This sweet, eggless biscuit uses rolled oats, butter and golden syrup, with coconut included in many familiar recipes.
foodDescriptions.Meat pie (Australia and New Zealand): The familiar individual meat pie encloses minced or diced meat and gravy in pastry.
foodDescriptions.Vegemite on toast: Vegemite adds a salty, savoury yeast-extract spread to buttered toast, usually in a thin layer.

new-zealand.intro: New Zealand's volcanic plateaus, caves and Southern Alps place very different landscapes within one island country. Māori heritage, contemporary cities and a distinctive filmmaking history add further layers to the journey.
new-zealand.tagline: Māori heritage, alpine scenery and imaginative journeys
new-zealand.languages: English, te reo Māori and New Zealand Sign Language

sources.title: Tourism New Zealand: Hobbiton Movie Set
Tourism New Zealand: Wellington Cable Car
Tourism New Zealand: Tongariro Alpine Crossing

attractionDescriptions.Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa: On Wellington's waterfront, Te Papa brings together collections and exhibitions about Aotearoa's people, art and natural environment. Māori taonga and stories sit alongside interpretations of the country's changing society.
attractionDescriptions.Wellington Botanic Garden: Paths on the hills above central Wellington connect gardens, native forest and viewpoints over the city. The cable car's Kelburn terminus provides a convenient starting point for exploring the grounds.
attractionDescriptions.Waitomo Glowworm Caves: Guided cave experiences reveal limestone formations and tiny lights produced by glowworm larvae. The dark underground setting makes the glowing colonies one of Waitomo's most distinctive natural sights.
attractionDescriptions.Hobbiton Movie Set: The film set occupies rolling farmland near Matamata in Waikato. Hobbit holes, gardens and other carefully maintained details recreate the Shire landscapes seen in The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit.
attractionDescriptions.Aoraki / Mount Cook: New Zealand's highest mountain rises in the Southern Alps within a national park of glaciers and alpine valleys. The landscape has deep significance in the traditions of Ngāi Tahu.

new-zealand.cultureIntro: Māori culture is central to Aotearoa's identity, with Waitangi, Whakarewarewa and Te Puia offering distinct historical and living cultural perspectives. Te reo Māori, carving and performance remain important forms of expression.
new-zealand.foodIntro: New Zealand's food traditions include Māori earth-oven cooking, local dairy and produce, and much-loved baking and confectionery.
new-zealand.activitiesIntro: A city cable car, a volcanic walking route and a canyon jet-boat experience reveal different sides of New Zealand.
new-zealand.nightlifeIntro: Wellington's Cuba Street and Courtenay Place are established areas for restaurants, bars, performance venues and evening city life.

activityDescriptions.Wellington Cable Car: Ride from Lambton Quay to Kelburn for city and harbour views, then explore the nearby Botanic Garden or Cable Car Museum.
activityDescriptions.Tongariro Alpine Crossing: Plan this demanding alpine day walk through volcanic terrain using current Department of Conservation guidance, suitable equipment and weather conditions.
activityDescriptions.Shotover Jet: Join an operated jet-boat trip through the Shotover River's narrow canyons near Queenstown, following the operator's participation requirements.

foodDescriptions.Hāngī: A traditional Māori hāngī cooks meat and vegetables slowly in an earth oven heated with hot stones.
foodDescriptions.Hokey pokey ice cream: Hokey pokey ice cream combines a creamy vanilla base with crunchy pieces of honeycomb toffee.
foodDescriptions.Pavlova: Pavlova is a meringue-based dessert topped with whipped cream and fruit and is popular in both New Zealand and Australia.
foodDescriptions.Lolly cake: This unbaked sweet combines crushed malt biscuits, condensed milk, butter and colourful lollies, commonly finished with a coating of coconut.

fiji.intro: Fiji's islands combine coral reefs and tropical coastlines with forested interiors and busy market towns. Indigenous iTaukei and Indo-Fijian traditions help shape the food, faiths and everyday life of this Pacific nation.
fiji.tagline: Island reefs, garden paths and shared cultural traditions

sources.title: Tourism Fiji: Introduction and quick facts
Tourism Fiji: Market foods and duruka
Tourism Fiji: Fiji Culture Village and lovo

attractionDescriptions.Fiji Museum: Within Suva's Thurston Gardens, the Fiji Museum explores the islands' archaeology and cultural histories. Exhibits introduce early seafaring settlement, iTaukei heritage and the experiences of Indo-Fijian communities.
attractionDescriptions.Thurston Gardens: These established botanical gardens form a leafy public space in Suva and contain the Fiji Museum. Their paths and tropical planting offer a quieter setting close to central civic landmarks.
attractionDescriptions.Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple: This colourful Hindu temple stands at the southern end of Nadi town. Its South Indian architectural forms and painted details reflect the religious and cultural heritage of Fiji's Indian communities.
attractionDescriptions.Garden of the Sleeping Giant: Set below the Sabeto hills near Nadi, this garden grew from actor Raymond Burr's orchid collection. Walking paths lead among orchids, tropical planting and shaded landscaped areas.
attractionDescriptions.Albert Park, Suva: Albert Park is a prominent open green space beside Suva's civic buildings and near Thurston Gardens. It has hosted sporting events and major public occasions, including Fiji's independence ceremony.

fiji.cultureIntro: Meke combines song, dance and storytelling in iTaukei tradition, while Navala's bure architecture and Suva's markets reveal other aspects of local life. Indo-Fijian communities contribute important religious and culinary traditions.
fiji.foodIntro: Fijian food brings together root crops, coconut, seafood and earth-oven cooking, alongside the spices and dishes of Indo-Fijian kitchens.
fiji.activitiesIntro: Reef excursions, surf viewing and Sabeto's geothermal pools offer varied ways to experience Fiji beyond its towns.
fiji.nightlifeIntro: Suva's restaurants and bars offer a city evening, while harbour views and cultural performances provide quieter ways to spend time after sunset.

activityDescriptions.Cloudbreak, Fiji: Watch this celebrated Mamanuca reef break from an organised boat outing; surfing here requires experience suited to powerful waves and shallow reef.
activityDescriptions.Great Astrolabe Reef: Arrange a guided snorkelling or diving excursion around Kadavu to explore reef habitats, with sites selected for your ability and current sea conditions.
activityDescriptions.Sabeto Hot Springs: Visit Sabeto's geothermal bathing area near Nadi to experience the mud pools and warm-water pools within the locally operated site.

foodDescriptions.Fijian lovo: A lovo cooks foods such as meat, fish and root vegetables in an earth oven heated with stones.
foodDescriptions.Fijian kokoda: Kokoda combines fish marinated in citrus juice with coconut milk and chopped vegetables and herbs.
foodDescriptions.Duruka Fiji: Duruka is the unopened flower of a sugarcane relative, often cooked in coconut milk or included in curry.
foodDescriptions.Fijian kava: Known locally as yaqona, this earthy drink is prepared from the roots of the kava plant mixed and strained with water.

samoa.intro: Samoa's volcanic islands hold lava fields, waterfalls and coastal villages surrounded by tropical vegetation. Fa'a Samoa, the Samoan way of life, gives family, community and cultural practice a central place in the country's identity.
samoa.tagline: Volcanic landscapes and the living traditions of Fa'a Samoa

sources.title: Samoa Tourism: Nature and walking experiences
US National Park Service: Samoan food culture
Museum of New Zealand Te Papa: Pisupo
Wikimedia Commons: Pisupo and supoketi photograph

attractionDescriptions.Robert Louis Stevenson Museum (Samoa): Stevenson's former Vailima home near Apia is now a museum set in gardens. It tells the story of the Scottish author's final years in Samoa, where he was known as Tusitala.
attractionDescriptions.To-Sua Ocean Trench: A deep natural swimming hole opens within tropical gardens at Lotofaga on Upolu's south coast. A steep ladder leads to the water, with the coastal setting adding to the site's distinctive appearance.
attractionDescriptions.Piula Cave Pool: This freshwater spring pool and cave formed in an old lava tube at Piula Theological College. Its clear water sits beneath the college chapel on Upolu's north coast.
attractionDescriptions.Saleaula Lava Fields: Lava from Mount Matavanu's 1905–1911 eruption engulfed villages on Savai'i. Visitors can see dark lava flows and partly buried church remains that document the eruption's effect on local communities.
attractionDescriptions.Sopoaga Falls: Sopoaga's waterfall drops into a lush valley near Lotofaga on Upolu. A garden path leads to the viewing area, with plants labelled in Samoan and by their scientific names.

samoa.cultureIntro: Fa'a Samoa places strong emphasis on family, community and respect. Siva dance, siva afi fireknife performance, siapo barkcloth and the ceremonial sharing of 'ava are distinct expressions of Samoan culture.
samoa.foodIntro: Samoan meals often combine taro or breadfruit with coconut, fish, pork or chicken, with umu cooking important for shared feasts.
samoa.activitiesIntro: Forest trails, volcanic coastal scenery and Savai'i's waterfalls offer ways to explore Samoa's island landscapes.
samoa.nightlifeIntro: Fiafia evenings bring together food, music and dance, often including siva afi; current programmes vary between venues.

activityDescriptions.Mount Vaea: Follow the forest trail from Vailima toward Robert Louis Stevenson's tomb and viewpoints over Apia, allowing for steep and slippery terrain.
activityDescriptions.O Le Pupu-Puʿe National Park: Explore the park's designated walking routes through tropical vegetation and along volcanic coastal scenery, using current local access guidance.
activityDescriptions.Afu Aau Waterfall: Visit this rainforest waterfall on southeastern Savai'i and spend time at its freshwater pool, observing local site rules and water conditions.

foodDescriptions.Samoan umu: An umu uses heated stones to cook a shared meal that can include taro, breadfruit, fish and meats.
foodDescriptions.Pisupo and supoketi: This meal combines canned corned beef and spaghetti, served with white rice.
foodDescriptions.Samoan kava: Called 'ava in Samoa, this drink made from the kava plant has a formal place in ceremonial hospitality.
foodDescriptions.Palusami and breadfruit: Palusami wraps coconut cream in young taro leaves for cooking, while starchy breadfruit provides a familiar accompaniment.

vanuatu.intro: Vanuatu's islands combine coral-fringed coastlines, freshwater blue holes and volcanic landscapes. Ni-Vanuatu kastom, including oral traditions, village customs and distinctive arts, remains an important part of life across the archipelago.
vanuatu.tagline: Blue holes, island coastlines and the traditions of kastom
vanuatu.languages: Bislama, English and French; many Indigenous island languages

Vanuatu Tourism Office: Food and drink

attractionDescriptions.National Museum of Vanuatu: The museum in Port Vila presents objects and stories from Vanuatu's diverse island cultures. Traditional arts, archaeology and sand drawing help introduce the knowledge preserved through the Vanuatu Cultural Centre.
attractionDescriptions.Mele Cascades: A sequence of cascades and natural pools lies in tropical vegetation near Mele on Efate. Walking paths reveal the stream and waterfall landscape beyond Port Vila's urban waterfront.
attractionDescriptions.Chief Roi Mata's Domain: This World Heritage cultural landscape links sites on Efate, Lelepa and Artok with the life and death of Chief Roi Mata. Archaeology and oral tradition together preserve the chief's enduring significance.
attractionDescriptions.Champagne Beach (Vanuatu): On Espiritu Santo, Champagne Beach curves around a bay with pale sand and clear blue water. Its coastal setting is one of the island's best-known natural landmarks.
attractionDescriptions.Erakor Island: This small island sits in a lagoon beside Efate near Port Vila. Beaches, palms and surrounding shallow-water habitats give it a different setting from the nearby capital's busy waterfront.

vanuatu.cultureIntro: Kastom carries ancestral knowledge through ceremonies, stories, art and community practice, with different traditions across Vanuatu's islands. Pentecost's nagol land diving and Vanuatu sand drawing are two distinctive examples.
vanuatu.foodIntro: Root crops, coconut cream, banana leaves and hot-stone cooking are central to ni-Vanuatu food, alongside seafood and dishes shaped by outside influences.
vanuatu.activitiesIntro: Snorkelling excursions and Santo's spring-fed blue holes offer ways to explore Vanuatu's marine and freshwater environments.
vanuatu.nightlifeIntro: Port Vila's waterfront offers evening dining and sunset views, while nakamals have a distinct place in the social tradition of sharing kava.

activityDescriptions.Hideaway Island: Arrange a snorkelling or diving visit to the marine setting off Mele Bay, where the underwater post box is a distinctive feature.
activityDescriptions.Blue Hole, Espiritu Santo: Visit Nanda's clear, spring-fed pool on Espiritu Santo, with tropical greenery around the water and places to pause beside it.
activityDescriptions.Nanda Blue Hole: Visit Nanda, also called Jackie's Blue Hole, to see intensely blue freshwater surrounded by tropical vegetation on Espiritu Santo.

foodDescriptions.Laplap: Laplap combines grated root crops such as taro, yam or cassava with coconut cream, traditionally wrapped in leaves and cooked with hot stones.
foodDescriptions.Vanuatu Beef Curry with Boiled Taro: Beef curry is served with boiled taro, a starchy root crop widely used in Pacific cooking.
foodDescriptions.Vanuatu Nem Spring Rolls: These Vanuatu-style nems are deep-fried spring rolls filled with minced beef.
foodDescriptions.Vanuatu kava: Vanuatu's kava drink is prepared from the plant's roots and water and is traditionally shared at gathering places known as nakamals.
